text: Module eleven. The administrative half of being a client.
Three roles. Owners administer; administrators and viewers read. And they are per organisation — the same colleague can own one account and merely view another.
A colleague is added by number, not by email, because the number is what they sign in with.

Two removals are simply refused, and the table says so rather than offering a button. Your own row reads You; a sole owner reads Only owner. Locking every human out of an account is a support request, not a click.
Settings splits the same way. Your name, your email, your language — yours to change.

The organisation's name and tax number are not. They are how finance and an auditor identify this account, so they change by asking us, with a record of who asked. An organisation cannot change its own status at all.
Underneath, the tier. Sapling, and a discount of nothing — which is the answer to a question module ten left open.
Because a discount is stamped on an order when it is placed. Reaching a new tier does not reprice what you already bought, and losing trees claws nothing back.
A certificate is the last of them, and the definition is the whole page: a certificate is a period, signed.
The record is immediate and the document follows — the column reads Preparing while the file is made.
And the staff side. Two kinds of organisation kept on separate tabs: accounts that buy trees, and partners that embed Otesha through the API.

With one number worth stopping on. Trees reads living over ordered — three hundred and six of three hundred and forty-six. The forty is the order placed while writing module ten, and it is the same outstanding figure the client sees on their own orders page.
One planned page is missing on purpose. The phone's More screen is navigation overflow, computed from the same config as the tab bar. There is no task on it.
Five pages. The account behind the trees.
